title: Power System Right Now
description: Production, flow, and balance on interconnectors right now in one-minute resolution.
comment:
**NOTE:** Data are based on upscaled realtime power measurements from the SCADA system. **Errors will occur, and will generally not be corrected.** For statistical purposes, see [Production and Consumption - Settlement](https://www.energidataservice.dk/tso-electricity/ProductionConsumptionSettlement).

---
**API Request Frequency** \
To get the most up-to-date data, calling the API with a dynamic timestamp such as [start=now-PT10M](https://api.energidataservice.dk/dataset/PowerSystemRightNow?start=now-PT10M) is a good approach. Making a request every minute or so is sufficient to ensure getting the latest data.
caution:
The following 4 columns have been deleted, as the data may be inaccurate due to new sources: 
* Imbalance DK1/DK2
* mFRR activated DK1/DK2. See instead [Realtime Electricity Market Data](https://www.energidataservice.dk/datasets/realtime-electricity-market).

Erroneous values occur in the column 'Production on plants less than 100 MW' from 2026-03-30 10.00 to 10.15 CET. The values will not be corrected.
author: Energinet

columns.description: UTC timestamp at which the values are valid.
columns.comment:
Please note that the _format_ shown in the example applies to data downloaded as JSON or fetched through the API.
The format is slightly different when it is shown on screen or downloaded manually as CSV or XLSX. This is mainly due to readability and consideration for Excel users.

**In preview (in the GUI)** all timestamps are shown as (display convention)
YYYY-MM-DD hh:mmZ
e.g. 2017-07-14 08:05Z. 
The Z will remind viewers that this is UTC.

In **download (CSV and XLSX)** the datetime is exported as
YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm
e.g. 2017-07-14 08:05.
That is without the “T” and the “Z” and the seconds. Excel will recognize it as date-time. The user must remember the convention about time zones.

In **download (JSON and API)** the datetime is exported as
YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss
e.g. 2017-07-14T08:05:00.
columns.validationRules: Always full minutes, i.e. seconds are 00

columns.description: Timestamp (in the _Danish time zone_) at which the values are valid.
columns.comment:
On one normal day there will be 24 * 60 = 1440 values.

When daylight saving times shifts there will be either 1380 or 1500 values.

Please note that the _format_ shown in the example applies to data downloaded as JSON or fetched through the API.
The format is slightly different when it is shown on screen or downloaded manually as CSV or XLSX. This is mainly due to readability and consideration for Excel users.

**In preview (in the GUI)** all timestamps are shown as (display convention)
YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm
e.g. 2017-07-14 08:00. 
Please note that there is no time zone indicator, showing that this is local (Danish) time.

In **download (CSV and XLSX)** the datetime is exported as
YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm
e.g. 2017-07-14 08:00.
That is without the “T” and the seconds. Excel will recognize it as date-time. The user must remember that this is local (Danish) time.

In **download (JSON and API)** the datetime is exported as
YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss
e.g. 2017-07-14T08:00:00.
columns.validationRules: Always full minutes, i.e. seconds are 00

Electricity production from Solar power.
columns.comment:
The estimated production is based on real-time measurements, occasionally containing small errors that are not corrected retroactively. Consequently, these estimates may deviate from actual production, such as instances of minimal nighttime solar panel output.

Negative values occur between November 27, 2025 and January 13th, 2026. The values will not be corrected.

columns.description:
Activated aFRR regulation in MW for price area DK1. 
Positive value indicates upward regulation need.
Negative value indicates downward regulation need.
columns.comment:
**Caution:** The column is part of the pilot phase: Realtime publication of imbalances. It is important to stress that this is a pilot phase aimed at confirming whether real time publication of imbalance volumes has a positive impact on system balancing.

Users of the dataset are advised that the realtime dataset may contain errors.
